statement.zh-TW: 速達機車行這一期的應付帳款增加了 {{money:vars.diff}}，表示有 {{money:vars.diff}} 的進貨還沒付錢；用間接法算營業活動的現金時，這 {{money:vars.diff}} 要加回來。
statement.en: Swift Scooter Repairs’ trade payables rose by {{money:vars.diff}} this period, meaning {{money:vars.diff}} of purchases has not yet been paid for; when working out operating cash by the indirect method, this {{money:vars.diff}} is added back.

feedbackTrue.zh-TW: 答對了。沒付出去的錢還留在帳戶裡，所以相對於利益，現金要多加這一筆。
feedbackTrue.en: That is right. Money not yet paid is still in the account, so cash is that much higher than profit suggests.

feedbackFalse.zh-TW: 欠的錢變多確實讓人覺得不太妙，這個直覺可以理解。不過間接法問的是「這一期實際付了多少現金」：應付帳款變多表示有一部分進貨還沒付，現金因此比利益算出來的多，所以要加回。
feedbackFalse.en: More owed does sound like bad news, and the instinct is understandable. But the indirect method asks how much cash was actually paid this period: a rise in payables means part of the purchases is still unpaid, so cash is higher than profit implies, and the amount is added back.

explanation.zh-TW: 「{{term:tm_dc0p0nrv}}」這一列的邏輯和應收帳款相反：應收帳款增加是「賣了沒收到」要扣，{{term:tm_a3p9y6kc}}增加是「買了沒付」要加。等下一期真的付款，應付帳款減少，那時才扣。
explanation.en: The logic of the {{term:tm_dc0p0nrv}} line is the mirror image of receivables: a rise in receivables means goods sold but not yet collected, so it is deducted; a rise in {{term:tm_a3p9y6kc}} means goods bought but not yet paid for, so it is added. When the bill is actually paid next period, payables fall and the deduction comes then.
